nodes.name: Hash-coded set membership testing with allowable errors
nodes.statement: Given a set $M$ of $n$ messages each $b$ bits long, design a hash-coded data structure of $N$ bits that, on a query message, returns 'member' or 'nonmember' while permitting a small false-positive fraction $P$, minimizing $N$ (space) and the expected reject time $T$.
nodes.statement_clean: Test messages for membership in a fixed set using a small hash area, allowing a controlled fraction of false positives in order to shrink the structure.

nodes.name: Allowable fraction of errors $P$
nodes.statement: $P = (n_a - n)/(n_t - n)$, where $n$ is the number of messages in the given set $M$, $n_a$ is the number of messages in the message space accepted as members, and $n_t$ is the total number of distinct messages in the message space.
nodes.statement_clean: The fraction of non-members of M that are erroneously accepted (false-positive rate).

nodes.name: Space factor $N$
nodes.statement: $N$ = total number of bits in the hash area.
nodes.statement_clean: The size of the hash area in bits.

nodes.name: Normalized time measure $T$
nodes.statement: $T = \mathrm{mean}_{m_i \in a}(t_i)$, the average number of bit-test units needed to reject a non-member, where the unit is the time to compute one hash bit-address, access that bit, and test it.
nodes.statement_clean: Expected per-message reject time, normalized to a single bit-address-and-test operation.

nodes.name: Normalized space measure $S$
nodes.statement_clean: Hash area size normalized by the information-theoretic lower bound for storing n keys with false-positive rate P.

nodes.name: Empty-cell fraction $\phi$ (conventional)
nodes.section: Analysis of the Conventional Hash-Coding Method
nodes.statement: $\phi = (h - n)/h = (N - n(b+1))/N$, the fraction of cells in the conventional hash area that remain empty after all $n$ messages have been stored.
nodes.statement_clean: Fraction of unused cells in the conventional hash table of h cells of (b+1) bits each.

nodes.name: Empty-cell fraction $\phi'$ (Method 1)
nodes.statement: $\phi' = (N' - n c)/N'$, where the hash area of $N'$ bits is organized into cells of $c$ bits each.
nodes.statement_clean: Fraction of empty cells in the Method-1 (smaller-cell coded) hash area.

nodes.name: Zero-bit fraction $\phi''$ (Method 2)
nodes.statement: $\phi'' = (1 - d/N'')^n$, the expected proportion of bits in a hash area of $N''$ bits still set to $0$ after $n$ messages have each set $d$ distinct bits to $1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Probability that a given bit of the Method-2 bit array is still 0 after all n insertions.

nodes.name: Conventional hash-coding method (error-free, baseline)
nodes.statement: Open-addressing hash table of $h$ cells of $b{+}1$ bits each (a flag bit plus the message); insertion probes pseudorandom cells until an empty one is found; lookup probes until a matching cell or an empty cell is encountered.
input: Set $M$ of $n$ messages, each $b$ bits long
Hash area of $h \ge n$ cells of $b+1$ bits
output: Cell array storing all messages of $M$
Membership test that returns 'accept' on match and 'reject' on first empty cell
nodes.pseudocode: Insert(m): k <- hash(m, 0); while cell[k] not empty do k <- hash(m, next); store m in cell[k]. Lookup(m'): k <- hash(m', 0); while cell[k] not empty do { if cell[k] = m' return accept; k <- hash(m', next) } return reject.

nodes.name: Method 1 (small-cell hash-coded with allowable errors)
nodes.section: Two Hash-Coding Methods with Allowable Errors
nodes.statement: Same open-addressing layout as the conventional method, but each cell stores only a $c$-bit code derived from the message ($c < b$); collisions of code values cause false positives whose rate decreases as $c$ grows.
input: Hash area of $N'$ bits organized into cells of $c$ bits
output: Cell array storing $c$-bit codes of all messages
Membership test with false-positive rate $\approx P'$
nodes.pseudocode: Insert(m): k <- hash(m, 0); while cell[k] not empty (first bit 1) do k <- hash(m, next); store code_c(m) in cell[k]. Lookup(m'): k <- hash(m', 0); while cell[k] not empty do { if cell[k] = code_c(m') return accept; k <- hash(m', next) } return reject.

nodes.name: Method 2 (Bloom filter)
nodes.section: Two Hash-Coding Methods with Allowable Errors
nodes.statement: Treat the hash area as $N''$ individually addressable bits; for each message hash to $d$ distinct bit-addresses $a_1,\dots,a_d$ and set those bits to $1$; on query, compute $a_1',\dots,a_d'$ and accept iff all $d$ bits are $1$.
input: Bit array of $N''$ bits initialized to 0
output: Bit array with at most $nd$ bits set
Membership test with false-positive rate $P'' = (1 - \phi'')^d$ and zero false-negative rate
nodes.pseudocode: Insert(m): for i = 1..d: bits[hash_i(m)] <- 1. Lookup(m'): for i = 1..d: if bits[hash_i(m')] = 0 return reject; return accept.

nodes.name: Conventional space/time trade-off
nodes.section: Analysis of the Conventional Hash-Coding Method
nodes.statement_clean: Hash-area size as a function of expected reject time T for the conventional (error-free) method.

nodes.name: Method 1 false-positive expression
nodes.statement: $P' = (\tfrac{1}{2})^{c-1}/\phi'$, equivalently $c = -\log_2 P' + 1 + \log_2\bigl(\tfrac{T'+2}{3}\bigr)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Expected false-positive rate of Method 1 in terms of code length c and empty-cell fraction; rearranged for c.

nodes.name: Method 1 three-factor trade-off
nodes.statement: $N' = n\Bigl(-\log_2 P' + 1 + \log_2\dfrac{T'+2}{3}\Bigr)\dfrac{T'+2}{T'-1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Joint relation among space, time and error fraction for Method 1.

nodes.name: Method 2 false-positive expression
nodes.statement: $P'' = (1 - \phi'')^d$ with $\log_2 \phi'' \approx -n(d/N'')\log_2 e$ and expected reject time $T'' = 1/\phi''$.
nodes.statement_clean: False-positive probability of Method 2 as a function of d, N'' and n.

nodes.name: Method 2 three-factor trade-off
nodes.statement_clean: Joint relation among space, time and error fraction for Method 2.

nodes.name: Normalized space curves $S'$, $S''$
nodes.statement_clean: Normalized space S = N/(-n log2 P) for Method 1 and Method 2.

nodes.name: Optimal operating point of Method 2
nodes.statement: For fixed $P''$, the normalized space $S''$ is minimized when $\phi'' = 1/T'' = 1/2$, i.e. when half the bits of the hash area are $1$ and half are $0$ (equivalently $T'' = 2$).
nodes.statement_clean: Method 2 is most space-efficient when each bit is set with probability 1/2.

nodes.name: Method 2 dominates Method 1
nodes.statement: For all admissible $T$ and $P$, $S'' < S'$, with $S' > (T'+2)/(T'-1)$ and $\lim_{P' \to 0} S' = (T'+2)/(T'-1)$; consequently Method 2 requires a strictly smaller hash area than Method 1 for the same expected reject time and false-positive rate.
nodes.statement_clean: Method 2 (the bit-array Bloom-filter scheme) achieves smaller normalized space than Method 1 across all parameter settings.
assumptions: Same time unit applies to both methods
conclusions: $S'' < S'$ for all $T, P$ in range

nodes.name: Method 1 attains zero errors when cell exceeds message length
nodes.section: Two Hash-Coding Methods with Allowable Errors
nodes.statement: When the cell width $c \ge b$ (so the per-cell code can encode the entire message), Method 1 degenerates to the conventional method and incurs no errors; thus Method 1 spans the regime $1 \gg P \gg 2^{-b}$.

nodes.name: Method 2 cannot reach zero errors
nodes.section: Two Hash-Coding Methods with Allowable Errors
nodes.statement: Because increasing $d$ past the diminishing-returns point raises the fraction of $1$-bits and hurts performance, Method 2 has a nonzero minimum-achievable false-positive rate for any fixed $N''$ and therefore cannot match the error-free regime that Method 1 attains as $c \to b$.

nodes.name: Constant-cost-per-bit assumption
nodes.statement: All analyses assume a constant unit cost to address, access and test a single bit; the superiority of Method 2 over Method 1 may not hold when multibit chunked memory access or expensive multi-hash address calculation are charged separately.

nodes.name: Automatic English-word hyphenation
nodes.statement: Apply Method 2 to a 50,000-word exception dictionary out of 500,000 words: with $T = 2$ and $P = 1/16$, the hash area shrinks from about $2{,}000{,}000$ bits (conventional, $T = 4$) to under $300{,}000$ bits, fitting in core and reducing disk accesses by ~84%.
nodes.statement_clean: Bloom-filter hyphenation example: a small in-core filter screens the 50k-word disk dictionary and avoids most disk accesses.

nodes.name: Hyphenation: trade-off table for varying $P$
nodes.section: Analysis of Hyphenation Sample Application (Table I)
nodes.statement: Table I tabulates Method-2 hash-area size and percentage of disk accesses saved versus allowable error fraction: $P = 1/2 \to N = 72{,}800$ bits, 45.0% saved; $1/4 \to 145{,}600$, 67.5%; $1/8 \to 218{,}400$, 78.7%; $1/16 \to 291{,}200$, 84.4%; $1/32 \to 364{,}000$, 87.2%; $1/128 \to 509{,}800$, 88.5% (last-row value as printed in the source).
nodes.statement_clean: Empirical table of hash-area size and disk-access savings as the allowable error fraction P decreases.
nodes.notes: Final row reads '509,800 bits, 88.5%' in the OCR'd source; the printed P value for that row is partially garbled in the PDF->text extraction.

nodes.name: Derivation of conventional space/time trade-off
nodes.section: Analysis of the Conventional Hash-Coding Method
nodes.statement: Decompose expected reject time by conditioning on whether a probed cell is empty (probability $\phi$) or occupied; bound the expected number $E$ of bits tested in an occupied non-matching cell by a geometric-tail sum $\sum_{x \ge 1}(x+1)(1/2)^x = 3$; solve $T = (1-\phi)(E+T) + \phi$ to obtain $T = 3/\phi - 2$, then substitute into $\phi = (N - n(b+1))/N$.

nodes.name: Setup: empty vs. occupied cell decomposition
nodes.statement: With probability $\phi$ a probed cell is empty (one bit tested) and with probability $1-\phi$ it is occupied by a non-matching message (an expected $E$ bits tested before rejection, after which the procedure restarts), giving $T = (1-\phi)(E+T) + \phi$.

nodes.name: Bound expected bits per occupied non-matching cell
nodes.statement: Conditional on an occupied non-matching cell, the first $b$ bits agree with probability $(1/2)^x$ for the first $x$ bits; for $b \gg 1$, $E \approx \sum_{x \ge 1}(x+1)(1/2)^x = 3$.

nodes.name: Solve for $T$ and substitute the empty-fraction identity
nodes.statement: Solving the recurrence yields $T = 3/\phi - 2$; combining with $\phi = (N - n(b+1))/N$ gives $N = n(b+1)(T+2)/(T-1)$.

nodes.name: Derivation of Method 1 trade-off
nodes.statement: Repeat the conventional analysis with cell width $c$ in place of $b+1$; a false positive needs both a code collision (probability $(1/2)^{c-1}$) and the colliding cell to appear earlier in the probe sequence than any empty cell (probability $1/\phi'$), giving $P' = (1/2)^{c-1}/\phi'$; solving for $c$ and combining with $\phi' = (N' - nc)/N'$ yields the trade-off.

nodes.name: Identify the two events causing a false positive
nodes.statement: A non-member is accepted iff (i) the test code matches a stored code (probability $(1/2)^{c-1}$ given the leading flag bit) AND (ii) this collision occurs before any empty cell in the probe sequence (probability $1/\phi'$).

nodes.name: Substitute into space-fraction identity
nodes.statement: Combining with $\phi' = (N' - nc)/N'$ produces $N' = n(-\log_2 P' + 1 + \log_2((T'+2)/3))(T'+2)/(T'-1)$.

nodes.name: Derivation of Method 2 trade-off
nodes.statement: Each of the $N''$ bits is independently still $0$ with probability $\phi'' = (1 - d/N'')^n$; taking $\log_2$ and using $d \ll N''$ gives $\log_2\phi'' \approx -n(d/N'')\log_2 e$; the expected number of bits tested before a $0$ is $T'' = 1/\phi''$; combining with $P'' = (1-\phi'')^d$ and eliminating $d, \phi''$ gives the stated relation.

nodes.name: Compute $\phi''$
nodes.statement: $\phi'' = (1 - d/N'')^n$; for $d \ll N''$, $\log_2\phi'' \approx -n(d/N'')\log_2 e$.

nodes.name: Compute $T''$
nodes.statement: The reject procedure tests bits one by one; $x$ bits are tested when the first $x-1$ are $1$ and the $x$-th is $0$, giving $T'' = \sum_{x \ge 1} x \phi''(1-\phi'')^{x-1} = 1/\phi''$.

nodes.name: Eliminate $d, \phi''$
nodes.statement: Using $P'' = (1-\phi'')^d$ together with $\phi'' = 1/T''$ and $\log_2\phi'' \approx -n(d/N'')\log_2 e$ yields $N'' = n(-\log_2 P'')\log_2 e / (\log_2(1/T'')\,\log_2(1-1/T''))$.

nodes.name: Optimum at $T'' = 2$
nodes.statement: For fixed $P''$, $S'' \propto 1/(\log_2(1/T'')\log_2(1-1/T''))$; treating $\phi'' = 1/T''$ as the variable, the denominator $\log_2\phi'' \cdot \log_2(1-\phi'')$ is maximized in absolute value when $\phi'' = 1/2$, giving the minimum $S'' = \log_2 e \approx 1.47$ at $T'' = 2$.
